questions.title: What to Do If Your Ball Is in a No Play Zone
questions.question: If your ball, your feet, or your swing are in a no play zone, what should you do?

choices.text: Hit your ball from there and forget about the no play zone.
Move your ball out for free; you are not allowed to hit from a no play zone.
Take a penalty before picking up your ball.
Ask your friends if you can play there.

questions.explanation: You must move your ball for free if it is in a no play zone, or if you would have to stand or swing there. You are not allowed to hit your ball from a no play zone.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course where you are not allowed to play your ball from at all.
Moving your ball to a new spot because of a special rule, often for free.

questions.teachingTip: Show children signs or markings for no play zones on a golf course. Practise taking relief together near a marked area.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can just play their ball from a no play zone if it is easier.
Some may believe they need to take a penalty to move their ball, but moving out of a no play zone is free.

questions.title: No Play Zones in Relief Situations
questions.question: If your ball, stance or swing is in a no play zone, what must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies and ignore the no play zone.
Take free relief; you are not allowed to play the ball as it lies.
Take a penalty stroke before moving the ball.
Ask your group for permission to play from there.

questions.explanation: You must take free relief if your ball, stance or swing is in a no play zone. Playing from there is not allowed under the rules.
